opening.argument: The presentation places an unusually concrete income promise beside a direct external destination: “Up To $800 Per Day” in “Totally Automated Crypto Profits” is followed by a shortened link. That is more than neutral market commentary; it gives viewers a financial outcome and an apparent next step for pursuing it. The same description also promotes joining “Crypto University,” while the video is framed around whether viewers should invest in NEAR. Taken together, the material can function as a solicitation to enter a crypto-related opportunity, even though the exact mechanics of the linked offer are not shown.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the link “separate” does not resolve its placement in the same description as the investment-focused video. The cited market-analysis heading describes a format, not the commercial effect of pairing crypto discussion with a high daily-profit claim and external links. Nor does the title merely ask an abstract question: it directly asks whether the viewer should invest this year.

The video also tells viewers to research independently and never risk more than they can afford to lose, so the cited pairing does not establish a deceptive investment mechanism.

opening.argument: The material repeatedly foregrounds monetary upside while using crypto-specific promotional cues. It describes possible value above $200 per coin, presents multiple future price figures, and advertises up to $800 per day in automated crypto profits through an external link. The visual sequence also labels the subject “INCREASING NEAR PROTOCOL” and displays “$200,” followed by a slide asking whether investing would be wise. This combination can make speculative appreciation and easy income feel actionable, rather than simply informing viewers about risk.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The disclaimer and risk language do not neutralize the overall emphasis on upside. A viewer sees a series of precise projections, including $3.84, $6.60, and $21.62, alongside an investment question; describing those figures as analysis does not make the promotional impression disappear. The warning that trends are not guaranteed still leaves the attractive return narrative prominent.

opening.argument: Although presented as an explainer, the content repeatedly steers the viewer toward considering participation. The title asks “Should You Invest This Year?”, the description calls NEAR a “smart investment opportunity,” and the narration asks whether investing would be a wise move. Future appreciation is then supplied through figures such as more than $200 per coin and projected values through 2030. That framing makes the educational wrapper serve as promotion for buying or holding the token, especially when paired with subscriptions, a crypto course link, and an automated-profit offer.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the word “analysis” as dispositive, but the surrounding framing is what matters. A purported explainer that asks whether viewers should invest, highlights dramatic future valuations, and directs viewers to crypto-related destinations can still steer participation. Calling the material entertainment does not change the practical invitation created by those repeated investment cues.
